🚨 Tech Mahindra SQL Interview Questions (3–5 Years Data Engineer)

If you can’t solve these…
You’re not interview-ready yet.

I came across these real-world SQL questions asked for a Data Engineer role (3–5 years experience).

Let’s see how strong your SQL fundamentals really are 👇

🔥 1️⃣ Top 3 Cities with Highest Sales Per Month

👉 Requires:
 • GROUP BY
 • Window functions
 • ROW_NUMBER()
 • Partitioning by month

If you don’t know how to use window functions properly, this one will expose you.


🔥 2️⃣ Running Total of Sales Per City

👉 Tests:
 • SUM() OVER()
 • PARTITION BY
 • ORDER BY inside window function

This is commonly used in analytics dashboards & financial reporting.

🔥 3️⃣ Second Highest Salary

👉 Multiple approaches:
 • DENSE_RANK()
 • Subquery with MAX()
 • TOP + ORDER BY
 • CTE method

Interviewers love this because it checks both logic & edge case handling.

🔥 4️⃣ Employees with Same Salary in Same Department

👉 Tests:
 • Self join
 • Window functions
 • Data grouping logic

This evaluates real relational thinking.

🔥 5️⃣ Find & Delete Duplicate Records

👉 Must know:
 • ROW_NUMBER()
 • CTE
 • Partition logic
 • Safe delete pattern

If you are a Data Engineer and you don’t know how to safely remove duplicates using CTE + ROW_NUMBER… that’s risky in production.

💡 What This Interview Actually Tests:

✔ Strong SQL fundamentals
✔ Window functions mastery
✔ Data cleaning skills
✔ Real-world data scenarios
✔ Performance awareness

This is not “basic SQL”.
This is production-level SQL thinking.

Now I want to test YOU 👇

👉 Which method do you prefer for finding the 2nd highest salary — and why?
👉 Would you use DENSE_RANK() or a subquery approach in production?

text:
The SQL Interview Trap: "Fetch every other row." 🛑
It sounds simple. Almost too simple.

📌 The Task:
You are given a Students table with 3 columns(ID,NAME and GENDER) with 10 rows. You want to find out and club every alternative record.

🛑The Input Table:
S1001 James M
S1002 Henry M
S1003 Emma F
...
🎯The Goal:
Write a query to find out alternate records(even and odd records) together.

📌The 3-Step "Bulletproof" Logic to solve this:
1️⃣Generate a Virtual Index: Use ROW_NUMBER(). This creates a perfect sequence (1, 2, 3...) regardless of how messy your underlying IDs are.
2️⃣The Modulus Filter: Apply the % (Modulus) operator to your new row number.
Row_Num % 2 = 0 → Even Rows
Row_Num % 2 <> 0 → Odd Rows
3️⃣The Wrapper: Since you can't filter a Window Function in a standard WHERE clause, wrap it in a CTE or a Subquery.

text:
Basic SQL question :
1. What happens if you use WHERE with NULL like this .
 
SELECT * FROM users 
WHERE city = NULL 

Output - This returns no rows because NULL cannot be compared using = .

So the current query will be - SELECT * FROM users
 WHERE city IS NULL

 2. If all 100 rows and 20 row containing NULL value . so what value
 COUNT(*) =? , 
COUNT(column_name) = ? 

COUNT(*) = 100 (It count total rows regardless NULL value)
 COUNT(column_name) = 80 (count all the non-null value )

Writing SQL query sometimes seems easy than understanding the basic SQL concepts .

text:
15 SQL Patterns Every Data Engineer Should Master
1. SELECT
 Core data retrieval for exploration, validation, and downstream transformations.
2. WHERE
 Filters rows early to reduce scan cost and improve pipeline performance.
3. ORDER BY
 Sorts datasets for ranking, audits, and time-based validations.
4. GROUP BY
 Aggregates metrics across dimensions like region, product, or customer.
5. HAVING
 Filters aggregated results after grouping — essential for KPI thresholds.
6. INNER JOIN
 Combines matching records across tables for fact–dimension modeling.
7. LEFT JOIN
 Enriches datasets while preserving all records from the primary table.
8. FULL OUTER JOIN
 Reconciles mismatches between systems during data comparisons.
9. DISTINCT
 Removes duplicates and validates uniqueness in raw ingestion layers.
10. CASE WHEN
 Adds business logic directly inside transformations and derived columns.
11. MERGE / UPSERT
 Powers incremental loads and CDC pipelines in modern warehouses.
12. WINDOW FUNCTIONS (OVER)
 Enables rankings, running totals, partitions, and advanced analytics.
13. SUBQUERIES
 Nest logic for conditional filtering and dependent calculations.
14. CTEs (WITH)
 Make complex transformations readable, modular, and easier to debug.
15. UNION / UNION ALL
 Combine datasets vertically across partitions or time ranges.
These aren’t just “SQL basics.”
They’re the foundation of:
• Reliable pipelines
 • Accurate dashboards
 • Scalable transformations
 • Clean analytics layers
 • Production-grade data platforms
Master these — and everything else in the stack becomes easier.
 Skip them — and no amount of tooling will save your pipelines.
If you’re building in Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or modern BI — this list is your daily toolkit.
Save this. Practice it. Revisit it often.
Because strong SQL is still your biggest leverage.
